This training site is intended for WBSC-certified Softball Umpires participating in the 2026-2029 accreditation and reaccreditation cycle.

Modern international softball moves faster than the mechanics built to officiate it once did. Sightlines shift mid-play. Batters and baserunners generate speed that compresses the time an umpire has to find the right angle, and defensive positioning has grown more varied, so plays develop in ways that reward anticipation as much as reaction.

The 2026-2029 Umpire Mechanics Program was revised to meet that reality. Every module in this pathway is built around one question umpires ask before every pitch - not only where to be, but why that position gives them the view the play requires.
That question runs through the whole system, but it is answered most directly in two documents.
Appendix 4 provides the why. Appendix 5 provides the how.
WBSC has reviewed and restructured its Softball Umpire Mechanics educational materials to provide a clearer, progressive learning pathway for umpires across all Regions and National Federations.

The framework is built around Four Connected Pillars, progressing from foundational umpiring principles and field mechanics through to advanced elite positioning philosophies and international field mechanics.

The revised structure separates foundational and elite learning while maintaining one consistent WBSC mechanics system, supported by common terminology, principles and standards. Each step builds on the one before it, so work through them in order.
Core umpiring principles that underpin every level of officiating.
One, two and three-umpire systems built on those foundations.
The reasoning, positioning philosophies and visual strategies behind elite officiating.
Advanced movement patterns and crew configurations up to six umpires.
Particular attention must be given to Appendices 4 and 5 and their accompanying presentations.
Elite mechanics are for students of the game and should only be introduced once an umpire has a strong command of the foundational material, not as a starting point.
Federations should confirm the equivalent guidance for their own accreditation pathway.
WBSC will use the Elite Teaching, Philosophies and Field Mechanics for all WBSC tournaments.
The Four Pillars support umpire education, accreditation and ongoing development, providing a common international reference for umpires, instructors, mentors and evaluators.

WBSC recognises that many National Federations already have well-established and comprehensive foundational umpire training programs. The revised framework is not intended to replace these programs or their existing educational materials. Rather, it provides a common international reference that complements and supports established development pathways.

The manuals are designed to be studied progressively. Elite mechanics build upon, rather than replace, established foundational mechanics, and are intended for experienced umpires with a strong understanding of the game.
Together, the Four Pillars support consistent umpire development and evaluation, from community softball through to elite WBSC international competition.

The six official publications of the 2026-2029 Umpire Mechanics Program, in the order they must be studied. Each module pairs the manual with its Manual Knowledge Check - read first, then check your understanding before moving on.

WBSC Softball Umpire Manual - Foundations Learning Guide. Version January 2026. Covers being an umpire, the Umpire Code of Ethics, core definitions, uniforms, pre-game preparation and game management.
Opens official WBSC publication in a new tab.
Confirms comprehension of the Foundations Learning Guide and reinforces the Code of Ethics and core terminology before you progress.

Appendix 1 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics FP: One-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. Dec 2025. Starting positions and mechanics for every runner and batted-ball combination in the one-umpire system, from no runners on through to bases loaded.
Confirms comprehension of one-umpire starting positions and coverage responsibilities before you progress.

Appendix 2 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics: Two-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. December 2025. The three basic principles of the two-umpire system, plate and base umpire starting positions, and mechanics for every runner and batted-ball combination.
Confirms comprehension of the two-umpire system's three basic principles and starting positions before you progress.

Appendix 3 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics: Three-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. January 2026. Introduces the Four Essential Elements and the Division and Infield/Outfield Principles, with plate and base umpire starting positions and outfield coverage for the three-umpire crew.
Confirms comprehension of the Four Essential Elements and three-umpire coverage principles before you progress to the elite material.
Appendix 4 provides the why · Appendix 5 provides the how
Elite mechanics are for students of the game and should only be introduced once an umpire has a strong command of the foundational material, not as a starting point.
Federations should confirm the equivalent guidance for their own accreditation pathway.
WBSC will use the Elite Teaching, Philosophies and Field Mechanics for all WBSC tournaments.
Appendix 4: Elite Umpire Mechanics, Positioning Philosophies

Appendix 4 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Elite Umpire Mechanics: Positioning Philosophies. April 2026. Key concepts and glossary, the principles behind dynamic positioning, optimising angle and distance, parallax error, and the visual discipline and cognitive-bias training that prepare umpires for Appendix 5.
Confirms comprehension of the elite positioning philosophies and key concepts before you move on to Appendix 5.
Appendix 5: Elite Three, Four, Five & Six-Umpire Field Mechanics

Appendix 5 (5a-5d) - WBSC Umpire Manual, Elite Field Mechanics FP: 3, 4, 5 & 6-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. February 2026. The Key Concepts Framework and Four Essential Element Theory (FEET), then position-by-position elite mechanics for the three-, four-, five- and six-umpire systems.
Optional practice on the elite field mechanics across the three- to six-umpire systems. The marked assessments are 5a, 5b and 5c, each taken after watching its presentation.

Each Manual Knowledge Check is unmarked practice: try it as often as you like to check your understanding before you continue. The corresponding training presentation is on the Presentations page, and each module's marked Presentation Competency Assessment is on the Assessments page.

What this temporary training site collects, why, who can see it, and how long it is kept.

This is a temporary training site, not the official WBSC website. The Softball Umpire Mechanics program is run by the WBSC Umpires Commission. The person responsible for the information described on this page is Leigh Evans, Director of Umpires, who can be contacted at umpiredirector@wbscoceania.org.

To take a marked Presentation Competency Assessment you enter your full name, email address, and optionally your Umpire ID and association or federation. We confirm that you control the email address by sending you a one-time code.

When you finish a marked assessment, this site records your name, verified email address, Umpire ID and association (if given), the module and assessment, your score and pass or not-passed result, which attempt it was, the date and time, and the program version. Nothing is recorded while you are still answering questions.
The Manual Knowledge Checks are practice only. You do not enter any details for them and nothing about them is recorded.

We email you a login code, and after each marked attempt a receipt showing your result and attempt number. The Director of Umpires receives a notice of each result and a notice when someone has passed all eight modules. These are service emails about your training record. We do not send marketing or newsletters.
Why we use it, and our basis

To confirm who took each assessment, apply the pass mark and the limit of two attempts, and keep a record that you completed the 2026-2029 accreditation and reaccreditation program. The basis is the legitimate interest of WBSC and its member federations in running and recording that program, and it is not used for advertising or sold. You can object or ask questions at any time.
Where it goes and who can see it

Results are saved as a row in a Google Sheet managed by the program administrator, and emails are sent through Gmail. The site uses Google Apps Script, Google Sheets and Gmail, so Google processes this information for us and may do so on servers outside your country. A login code (10 minutes) and a login session (6 hours) are held temporarily in Google Apps Script’s short-term cache and then expire; the code is kept only as a one-way hash, not as plain text.

Access is limited to the program administrator and the Director of Umpires. The Director can view results on a password-protected page. Results are not published or shared with other organisations by this site.

Results are kept for the length of the 2026-2029 program cycle and for two years after it ends, that is until the end of 2031. After that they are deleted, or kept only as anonymous totals that do not identify anyone. The notification emails sent to the Director of Umpires are deleted on the same schedule. Emails in your own inbox are yours to keep or delete.
Cookies and what is kept on your device

This site does not set cookies and does not use analytics, advertising or tracking. The fonts are served from this site, so your browser does not contact Google or any other third party to load a page.

While you are using the site, your browser keeps the details you typed and your login session in its session storage for that visit only; it is cleared when you close the tab. After you press OK on the cookies notice, or choose a language, that choice is remembered in your browser so that the notice is not shown again and the site opens in your language. If you stop a marked assessment part-way, your progress (the question you reached, your score so far and the order of the answer options) is also kept in your browser for up to 24 hours so you can resume on the same device; it is removed when you finish or choose to start again. That is all this site stores on your device. If you share a computer, choose “Start again” or clear your browser data.

When you request a login code or save a result, your browser sends the request to Google. Google receives technical information such as your IP address and may set its own cookies when it does; this is governed by Google’s own terms and privacy policy. The manuals and presentations are held on Google Drive and open in a new tab; Google handles those pages under its own policies.

Results are only recorded after your email address has been confirmed, the pass mark and attempt limit are applied on the server, and the Director’s results page needs a password. No system is perfectly secure. If we become aware of a breach that affects your information, the Director of Umpires will tell the people affected and the relevant authorities where the law requires.

You can ask what is held about you, ask for a result to be corrected or deleted, or object to how it is used. Contact Leigh Evans, Director of Umpires, at umpiredirector@wbscoceania.org. If you are not satisfied with the answer, you can complain to the privacy regulator in your own country or state.

Appendix 1 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics FP: One-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. Dec 2025. Starting positions and mechanics for every runner and batted-ball combination in the one-umpire system, from no runners on through to bases loaded.

Appendix 2 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics: Two-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. December 2025. The three basic principles of the two-umpire system, plate and base umpire starting positions, and mechanics for every runner and batted-ball combination.

Appendix 3 - WBSC Umpire Manual, Field Mechanics: Three-Umpire Systems, Learning Guide. January 2026. Introduces the Four Essential Elements and the Division and Infield/Outfield Principles, with plate and base umpire starting positions and outfield coverage for the three-umpire crew.
Confirms comprehension of the Four Essential Elements and three-umpire coverage principles before you progress to the elite material.

Appendix 4: Elite Umpire Mechanics, Positioning Philosophies

Key concepts and glossary, the principles behind dynamic positioning, optimising angle and distance, parallax error, and the visual discipline and cognitive-bias training that prepare umpires for Appendix 5.

What this temporary training site collects, why, who can see it, and how long it is kept.

This is a temporary training site, not the official WBSC website. The Softball Umpire Mechanics program is run by the WBSC Umpires Commission. The person responsible for the information described on this page is Leigh Evans, Director of Umpires, who can be contacted at umpiredirector@wbscoceania.org.

To take a marked Presentation Competency Assessment you enter your full name, email address, and optionally your Umpire ID and association or federation. We confirm that you control the email address by sending you a one-time code.

When you finish a marked assessment, this site records your name, verified email address, Umpire ID and association (if given), the module and assessment, your score and pass or not-passed result, which attempt it was, the date and time, and the program version. Nothing is recorded while you are still answering questions.
The Manual Knowledge Checks are practice only. You do not enter any details for them and nothing about them is recorded.

We email you a login code, and after each marked attempt a receipt showing your result and attempt number. The Director of Umpires receives a notice of each result and a notice when someone has passed all eight modules. These are service emails about your training record. We do not send marketing or newsletters.
Why we use it, and our basis

To confirm who took each assessment, apply the pass mark and the limit of two attempts, and keep a record that you completed the 2026-2029 accreditation and reaccreditation program. The basis is the legitimate interest of WBSC and its member federations in running and recording that program, and it is not used for advertising or sold. You can object or ask questions at any time.
Where it goes and who can see it

Results are saved as a row in a Google Sheet managed by the program administrator, and emails are sent through Gmail. The site uses Google Apps Script, Google Sheets and Gmail, so Google processes this information for us and may do so on servers outside your country. A login code (10 minutes) and a login session (6 hours) are held temporarily in Google Apps Script’s short-term cache and then expire; the code is kept only as a one-way hash, not as plain text.

Access is limited to the program administrator and the Director of Umpires. The Director can view results on a password-protected page. Results are not published or shared with other organisations by this site.

Results are kept for the length of the 2026-2029 program cycle and for two years after it ends, that is until the end of 2031. After that they are deleted, or kept only as anonymous totals that do not identify anyone. The notification emails sent to the Director of Umpires are deleted on the same schedule. Emails in your own inbox are yours to keep or delete.
Cookies and what is kept on your device

This site does not set cookies and does not use analytics, advertising or tracking. The fonts are served from this site, so your browser does not contact Google or any other third party to load a page.

While you are using the site, your browser keeps the details you typed and your login session in its session storage for that visit only; it is cleared when you close the tab. After you press OK on the cookies notice, or choose a language, that choice is remembered in your browser so that the notice is not shown again and the site opens in your language. If you stop a marked assessment part-way, your progress (the question you reached, your score so far and the order of the answer options) is also kept in your browser for up to 24 hours so you can resume on the same device; it is removed when you finish or choose to start again. That is all this site stores on your device. If you share a computer, choose “Start again” or clear your browser data.

When you request a login code or save a result, your browser sends the request to Google. Google receives technical information such as your IP address and may set its own cookies when it does; this is governed by Google’s own terms and privacy policy. The manuals and presentations are held on Google Drive and open in a new tab; Google handles those pages under its own policies.

Results are only recorded after your email address has been confirmed, the pass mark and attempt limit are applied on the server, and the Director’s results page needs a password. No system is perfectly secure. If we become aware of a breach that affects your information, the Director of Umpires will tell the people affected and the relevant authorities where the law requires.

You can ask what is held about you, ask for a result to be corrected or deleted, or object to how it is used. Contact Leigh Evans, Director of Umpires, at umpiredirector@wbscoceania.org. If you are not satisfied with the answer, you can complain to the privacy regulator in your own country or state.
